notes: Trilingual ceramic-tile street sign in the Armenian Quarter of Jerusalem Old City (East Jerusalem), slightly from below. Hebrew is pointed (niqqud as seen: shva under ר and מ, tsere under ג, patah under ה, qamats and dagesh in ק, holam on ו, shin dot); the geresh marks after ח and ג are written as ׳. notes: British Mandate-era trilingual ceramic tile sign on the Jaffa Gate wall, Jerusalem Old City, seen from below. The E of GATE is chipped and may OCR as F. The Arabic is in thuluth calligraphy with many small decorative marks (harakat-like ornaments) that are not transcribed. Maker's mark at bottom right is not transcribed. Location note: East Jerusalem may fall under Israel in some map extracts.

author: Godot13
attribution: Photo: Godot13, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons. Source: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Jerusalem-2013-Islamic_Museum_(sign).jpg. License: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. Unmodified original.

lines.latin: Mathaf al-Athar al-Islamiyya (Museum of Islamic Antiquities)

notes: Two framed boards on the wall of the Islamic Museum at al-Aqsa compound, Jerusalem Old City. The Arabic is stacked thuluth calligraphy full of small decorative marks (ornamental harakat), so hamza/madda signs cannot be told apart from ornaments; the line is given in standard spelling and an OCR reading may legitimately differ on those marks. The Hebrew rules notice at left is a distractor. Location note: East Jerusalem may fall under Israel in some map extracts. location is where the photo was taken (Commons camera coordinates), not the target.
source_categories: Exteriors of museums in the State of Palestine

lines.latin: Jami' anwa' al-ma'kulat (All kinds of food)

notes: Faded projecting restaurant sign in Ramallah, photographed from below, with a Nefertiti bust image. The name uses ڤ (veh, three dots above) not ف: نڤرتيتي; a search would likely use ف. The two 'أهلاً وسهلاً' greetings at the top carry a tanween mark. The bottom yellow script line (استعداد تام لتلبية جميع مناسباتكم...) is crossed by a bracket and is not transcribed. Pink sign below is a distractor.
